```plato
//==
// # Angles
//
// Sections, in order:
//  - Angles
//  - The public trigonometric surface on `Angle`

library Angles
{
    //==
    // # Angles
    //
    // Unit constructors and accessors for `Angle` (`quantities.types.plato`), plus the
    // reciprocal trigonometric functions (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trigonometric_functions).
    //
    // `Angle` stores radians and the only intrinsic way to build one is the
    // radians cast `Angle(x: Number)` (`intrinsics.library.plato`). This library supplies
    // the other units, in both directions, so that the README rule "angles are
    // `Angle`, never raw `Number`" is actually usable: write `0.25.Turns` or
    // `90.Degrees`, never a bare number of degrees.

    //==
    // Number -> Angle constructors

    // The angle spanning the given fraction of a full revolution.
    // 1.0.Turns is a full circle. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turn_(angle))
    Turns(x: Number): Angle
        => Angle(x * Number.Tau);
```

```plato
    //==
    // Integer -> Angle constructors
    //
    // Convenience overloads so that whole-number literals read naturally
    // (`90.Degrees`, `2.Turns`).

    // The angle spanning the given whole number of full revolutions.
    Turns(x: Integer): Angle
        => x.ToNumber.Turns;
```

## Line 75

**Source:** [stdlib/foundation/angles.library.plato, line 75](../../../../../stdlib/foundation/angles.library.plato#L75).

```plato

    //==
    // Angle -> Number accessors
    //
    // The inverse of the constructors above. Not normalized: an angle larger
    // than a full revolution reports more than one turn, and negative angles
    // report negative unit counts.

    // The angle measured in full revolutions.
    Turns(x: Angle): Number
        => x.Radians / Number.Tau;
```
